spec: VIGIL plan parsed-popping-lemur.md §4.2 (threat register), §4.1 (zones/boundaries), §4.3 (what stays trustworthy), §4.4 (origin and edge-chain declarations), §4.7 (publication).

publication_policy.rule: This repository is public. Per plan §4.7 only fixed-state governance is published: entries whose mitigation is a decided, committed architecture decision or a shipped control. Open / un-mitigated entries are NOT published here.
publication_policy.public: aegis-threat-model.json and aegis-threat-model.md — fixed state only.
publication_policy.private: Open entries live in the private handoff register (vigil-handoff), per plan §4.7 and the publication rule (HANDOFF:83).
publication_policy.drift_test: Plan §4.7 requires a drift test asserting every threat id exists in exactly one of the two registers (public or private).
publication_policy.as25_gate: Plan §4.7 line 639: an entry may be marked 'mitigated' only with a current AS-25 demonstration record (§13.3). In this AS-0 governance publication, record_ref makes the record state explicit: a shipped engineering record (e.g. 'AS-27a / PR#1228'), or 'pending-AS-25' where the decided mitigation's signed AS-25 demonstration record is scheduled but not yet built.

status_vocabulary.mitigated: Fixed state: either a shipped control with an engineering record, or a decided-and-committed architecture decision. This is the only status permitted in the public register; open threats are omitted (they stay in the private register).

record_ref_semantics.AS-27a / PR#1228: Shipped: the break-glass fail-open fixes merged in slice AS-27a (first gateway PR), covered by framework/v2/aegis/tests/test_gateway_breakglass.py.
record_ref_semantics.pending-AS-25: Decided and committed architecture whose signed AS-25 demonstration record (§13.3) is scheduled but not yet built. The drift/DONE gate will require the AS-25 record before the entry is demonstration-complete.

private_register_note: This file is the PUBLIC threat register and carries only fixed-state (mitigated / decided-and-committed) entries. Open, un-mitigated, or sensitive threat entries are maintained in the private handoff register (vigil-handoff) per plan §4.7; they are intentionally absent here. When an open entry is closed by a decided mitigation it is moved into this file described as the DECISION and the MITIGATION, never as a live weakness. The following DECIDED-but-not-yet-shipped threats are kept in the private register until their slice ships and earns an engineering/AS-25 record, at which point they move here: AEGIS-T-PXY-EDGE, AEGIS-T-XO-BIND, AEGIS-T-ISO-UNIT (edge routing AS-2d, origin binding AS-2g, unit isolation AS-2j).

threats.title: Break-glass kill-switch unreadable must not keep the gateway blocking
threats.attacker: A4 operator or A3 RCE-in-unit, or a control-plane read fault
threats.vector: The enforce gate consults the kill-switch (break-glass) subsystem; a read, import, or path fault on that subsystem leaves the enforce decision ambiguous, and reading it as CLEAR would keep the gateway blocking on a switch it cannot read.
threats.mitigation: AS-27a makes the gateway wrapper treat an unreadable kill-switch subsystem (is_tripped raising, or KillSwitch construction failing) as TRIPPED, so enforcement drops to pass-through rather than continuing to block on a switch it cannot read. The downgrade is honest: enforcement_status() reports enforcing=false, kill_switch_tripped=true, downgraded=true, and names the kill-switch as the downgrade reason. Register alias T-BG / T-FO; TT-STG negative 'unreadable kill switch -> no block'.

threats.title: Break-glass mode-file glitch must not silently escalate to enforce
threats.attacker: A4 operator, or a control-plane / filesystem fault
threats.vector: The gateway reads a live mode-override control file; a present-but-unreadable file (permission error, a directory at the path, a path-subsystem failure) is ambiguous, and treating it as 'no override' would fall through to the startup --mode, which may be enforce.
threats.mitigation: AS-27a classifies a present-but-unreadable mode file as a glitch, not 'no override': it falls back to the last cleanly-read override, and if none to OBSERVE — it never silently escalates to the startup --mode. A cleared or invalidated override is not resurrected by a later glitch (cache-invalidation guard). ENOENT/ENOTDIR are treated as 'absent' (startup mode, cache cleared); EACCES and a path-subsystem failure are glitches (hold last-known-good, else observe).
